content: 1. Strengthening routine data collection is essential for improving the impact of health programs, particularly in the context of HIV and other health services. This involves using cascade data to identify gaps in service delivery and implementing targeted improvements. 2. A manual for cascade data use was developed in 2018 to help identify deficiencies in HIV and health services, enabling programmatic enhancements. 3. The strategic framework for HIV self-testing, published in 2018, provides guidance on planning, introducing, and scaling up self-testing initiatives. This framework emphasizes the importance of integrating self-testing into broader health strategies. 4. The World Health Organization (WHO) has developed an implementation tool for pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) of HIV infection, with a specific module on monitoring and evaluation published in 2018. This tool supports the effective rollout and assessment of PrEP programs. 5. Consolidated guidelines on HIV prevention, testing, treatment, service delivery, and monitoring were published by WHO to provide recommendations for a public health approach. These guidelines aim to streamline and enhance HIV-related healthcare services. 6. The revolving door phenomenon in HIV care, where patients disengage and re-engage with services, has been analyzed to revise service delivery models and achieve the UNAIDS 95-95-95 goals. This involves ensuring that 95% of people living with HIV know their status, 95% of those diagnosed receive treatment, and 95% of those on treatment achieve viral suppression. 7. Research in Zambia has explored factors and mechanisms that enable patients to return to HIV care after disengagement. Understanding these trajectories is critical for improving re-engagement strategies. 8. A systematic review has examined the impact of HIV counseling and testing on HIV acquisition in sub-Saharan Africa, highlighting the importance of these services in reducing transmission rates. 9. Behavioral changes following HIV testing services have been systematically reviewed and analyzed, demonstrating the effectiveness of these services in promoting safer sexual practices. 10. Counseling and behavioral interventions for HIV, sexually transmitted infections (STIs), and viral hepatitis among key populations have been systematically reviewed for their effectiveness, values, preferences, and cost implications. 11. Recommendations for couples' HIV testing and counseling, including the use of antiretroviral therapy for treatment and prevention in serodiscordant couples, have been developed to support a public health approach. 12. A systematic review and meta-analysis have assessed the HIV status of discordant couples in sub-Saharan Africa, providing insights into the dynamics of transmission and prevention within these partnerships. 13. Interventions to prevent hepatitis C virus infection among people who inject drugs have been systematically reviewed and analyzed, offering evidence-based strategies for reducing transmission in this high-risk population. 14. WHO has updated its guidance on differentiated and simplified PrEP delivery for HIV prevention, emphasizing the need for tailored approaches to meet diverse population needs. 15. Recommendations for hepatitis C virus self-testing have been published, providing guidance on integrating self-testing into broader health strategies. 16. Dual HIV/syphilis rapid diagnostic tests are recommended as the first-line test in antenatal care settings, streamlining the diagnosis and management of these infections. 17. Guidelines on HIV self-testing and partner notification have been developed as a supplement to the consolidated guidelines on HIV testing services, emphasizing the role of self-testing in expanding access to diagnosis. 18. Consolidated guidelines on the use of antiretroviral drugs for treating and preventing HIV infection have been updated to reflect a public health approach, focusing on accessibility and effectiveness. 19. A counseling framework for HIV-serodiscordant couples has been developed to integrate the use of antiretroviral therapy and PrEP for HIV prevention, supporting comprehensive care strategies. 20. Differentiated service delivery models for HIV prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and care for key populations have been consolidated into guidelines to address the unique needs of these groups. 21. A scoping review has explored effective post-test linkage strategies for HIV prevention and care, identifying best practices for connecting individuals to necessary services. 22. Delivery arrangements for health systems in low-income countries have been systematically reviewed, providing an overview of strategies to improve service delivery in resource-limited settings. 23. A systematic review and meta-analysis have examined linkage to HIV care following diagnosis in the WHO European Region, identifying gaps and opportunities for improvement. 24. Interventions to improve the rate and timing of antiretroviral therapy initiation in sub-Saharan Africa have been systematically reviewed, highlighting effective strategies for accelerating treatment uptake. 25. A systematic review and meta-analysis have assessed interventions to improve linkage along the HIV-tuberculosis care cascades in lowand middle-income countries, providing evidence for integrated care approaches. 26. A decision framework for differentiated antiretroviral therapy delivery for key populations has been developed to guide programmatic decisions and optimize service delivery. 27. Differentiated HIV testing services should focus on diagnosing and linking individuals to care, particularly those unaware of their status or at substantial risk of HIV acquisition. Testing services should also integrate with other health services, such as STI and hepatitis screening. 28. Decentralization of HIV testing services, task sharing, and the use of trained lay providers are recommended to expand access and improve service delivery, particularly in community settings. 29. Self-testing for HIV, hepatitis C, and syphilis is recommended as an important tool for integrated service delivery, with potential applications in community-based, facility-based, and network-based testing services. 30. Differentiated HIV testing services should be client-centered, focusing on linking diagnosed individuals to treatment and those testing negative to effective prevention services, such as PrEP.
